extracted.intended_audience: Covered entities operating health programs or activities (e.g., State agencies, hospitals, clinics, health insurance issuers, Exchanges, MCOs, PACE organizations) required to comply with HHS Section 1557 nondiscrimination regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and programmatic standards that covered entities must implement to comply with Section 1557 (nondiscrimination in health programs or activities), including nondiscrimination policies, coordinators, language access, effective communication, grievance procedures, recordkeeping, and definitional standards. This covers both procedural obligations (assurances, deadlines, implementation of policies) and substantive definitions of terms (qualified interpreter, auxiliary aids, federal financial assistance, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: MCO/PIHP/PAHP/PCCM nondiscrimination contract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The MCO, PIHP, PAHP, PCCM or PCCM entity will not discriminate against individuals eligible to enroll on the basis of race; color; national origin; disability; or sex which includes sex characteristics, including intersex traits; pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity; and sex stereotypes; and will not use any policy or practice that has the effect of discriminating on the basis of [those protected characteristics].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed in §438.3(d)(4) as a standard contract requirement; applies to managed care organizations and related entities under part 438.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCO access and cultural considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP participates in the State's efforts to promote the delivery of services in a culturally competent manner to all enrollees, including those with limited English proficiency and diverse cultural and ethnic backgrounds, disabilities, and regardless of sex (including sex characteristics, ... sexual orientation, gender identity and sex stereotypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed in §438.206(c)(2); ties managed care plans into State efforts to promote culturally competent service delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: State methods to promote culturally competent service delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must have methods to promote access and delivery of services in a culturally competent manner to all beneficiaries, including those with limited English proficiency, diverse cultural and ethnic backgrounds, disabilities, and regardless of sex (including sex characteristics, ... sexual orientation, gender identity, and sex stereotypes). These methods must ensure that beneficiaries have access to covered services that are delivered in a manner that meets their individualized needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codified at §440.262; requires States to adopt concrete methods ensuring culturally competent, individualized service delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: State assurance of culturally competent access (Medicaid allotments/grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: State assurance of access to care and procedures to assure quality and appropriateness of care must include access to and delivery of services in a culturally competent manner to all beneficiaries, as described in 42 CFR 440.262.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added at §457.495(e); ties grant/allotment assurances to cultural competence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PACE nondiscrimination in service delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The PACE organization shall not discriminate against any participant in the delivery of required PACE services based on race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex (including sex characteristics, ... sexual orientation, gender identity, and sex stereotypes), age, mental or physical disability, or source of payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codified at §460.98(b)(3); applies specifically to Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PACE participant right to respectful, nondiscriminatory care
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participant has the right to considerate, respectful care from all PACE employees and contractors at all times and under all circumstances. Each participant has the right not to be discriminated against in the delivery of required PACE services based on [listed protected characteristics].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §460.112(a); part of participants' specific rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and purpose: implementation of Section 1557 nondiscrimination prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: This part implements section 1557 of the ACA, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, and disability in certain health programs and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined in §92.1(a); establishes the legal baseline and covered protected characteristics for the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance effective dates and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations in this part are effective beginning July 5, 2024, with specific compliance deadlines for particular provisions (e.g., §92.7 within 120 days; §92.8 within one year; certain §92.207 provisions by the first day of the first plan year beginning on or after Jan 1, 2025; §92.210(b) and (c) within 300 days, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 to paragraph (b) in §92.1(b) lists section-specific timelines and phased compliance dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: entities and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: This part applies to every health program or activity any part of which receives Federal financial assistance from the Department; every health program or activity administered by the Department; and every health program or activity administered by a title I entity. The provisions do not apply to any employer or other plan sponsor of a group health plan with regard to its employment practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.2; distinguishes covered entities and identifies an explicit employment-practices exclusion for plan sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to other laws and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither section 1557 nor this part shall be construed to apply a lesser standard for protection than standards under title VI, title IX, the Age Discrimination Act, or section 504. Nothing in this part invalidates or limits rights, remedies, procedures, or legal standards under those laws. Applications that would violate Federal protections for religious freedom and conscience are not required. Nothing supersedes state or local laws that provide additional protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.3; clarifies interaction with other civil rights laws and enumerates exceptions and non-preemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: auxiliary aids and services (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary aids and services include, for example: (1) qualified interpreters on-site or through VRI; note takers; real-time transcription; written materials; exchange of written notes; assistive listening devices; telecommunications products; videophones; accessible ICT; (2) qualified readers; taped texts; audio recordings; Braille materials; screen reader software; magnification; optical readers; SAP; large print materials; accessible ICT; (3) acquisition or modification of equipment and devices; and (4) other similar services and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; provides concrete examples that covered entities must consider when ensuring effective communication for persons with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: federal financial assistance (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal financial assistance means any grant, loan, credit, subsidy, contract (other than a procurement contract but including a contract of insurance), or other arrangement by which the Federal Government directly or indirectly provides assistance, including funds, services of Federal personnel, or real or personal property or interest in such property (including transfers/leases below fair market value and proceeds where federal share is not returned). It also includes Department-administered assistance (e.g., advance payments of premium tax credit and cost-sharing reductions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.4; determines whether an entity or program falls within the part's coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: health program or activity (scope of operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Health program or activity means any project, enterprise, venture, or undertaking to provide or administer health-related services, health insurance coverage, assistance to persons obtaining services or coverage, clinical/pharmaceutical/medical care, health or clinical research, or health education; and includes all operations of any entity principally engaged in such activities (e.g., State/local health agency, hospital, clinic, insurer, physician's practice, pharmacy, nursing facility, residential or community-based treatment facility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined in §92.4(1)–(2); used to determine the operational scope covered by Section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: individual with limited English proficiency (LEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual whose primary language for communication is not English and who has a limited ability to read, write, speak, or understand English; may be competent for some communications but limited for others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; used to determine language assistance obligations in §92.201 and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: information and communication technology (ICT)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICT means information technology and other equipment, systems, technologies, or processes whose principal function is creation, manipulation, storage, display, receipt, or transmission of electronic data and information, and includes computers, kiosks, telehealth interfaces, software, mobile apps, websites, videos, and electronic documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; relevant for ICT accessibility requirements (see §92.204).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: language assistance services (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Language assistance services may include: (1) oral language assistance, interpretation in non-English languages in-person or remotely by a qualified interpreter and use of qualified bilingual/multilingual staff; (2) written translation performed by a qualified translator of written content in paper or electronic form; and (3) written notice of availability of language assistance services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; sets examples of services that satisfy LEP obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: machine translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Machine translation means automated translation, without assistance of or review by a qualified human translator, that is text-based and provides instant translations between various languages, sometimes with an option for audio input or output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; distinguishes automated solutions from qualified human translation where human review may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: national origin (broad interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: National origin includes, but is not limited to, a person's, or their ancestors', place of origin (such as country or world region) or a person's manifestation of the physical, cultural, or linguistic characteristics of a national origin group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; clarifies scope of national origin protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: qualified bilingual/multilingual staff
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of a covered entity's workforce designated by the covered entity to provide in-language oral language assistance as part of assigned job responsibilities and who has demonstrated: (1) proficiency in speaking and understanding both English and at least one other spoken language, including specialized vocabulary/terminology; and (2) ability to effectively, accurately, and impartially communicate directly with individuals with LEP in their primary languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; establishes baseline for designating bilingual staff to provide language assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: qualified interpreter for individuals with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An interpreter who, via VRI or on-site appearance: (1) has demonstrated proficiency in communicating in and understanding both English and a non-English language (including ASL or other sign languages) or another communication modality; (2) is able to interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially, receptively and expressively, using necessary specialized vocabulary without changes, omissions, or additions and while preserving tone/sentiment/emotional level; and (3) adheres to generally accepted interpreter ethics including client confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; lists specific performance and ethical expectations for interpreters serving individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: qualified interpreter for LEP individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: An interpreter who, via remote interpreting service or on-site appearance: (1) has demonstrated proficiency in speaking and understanding English and at least one other spoken language (for relay, proficiency in two non-English languages); (2) can interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially to and from such language(s) and English (or between two non-English languages for relay), using necessary specialized vocabulary without changes, omissions, or additions and while preserving tone/sentiment/emotional level; and (3) adheres to generally accepted interpreter ethics including confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; sets standards for interpreters used to provide oral language assistance to LEP persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: qualified reader
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is able to read effectively, accurately, and impartially using any necessary specialized vocabulary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; applies where reading assistance is necessary for effective communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: qualified translator
rubrics_metrics.description: A translator who: (1) has demonstrated proficiency in writing and understanding both written English and at least one other written non-English language; (2) is able to translate effectively, accurately, and impartially to and from such language(s) and English, using necessary specialized vocabulary without changes, omissions, or additions and while preserving tone/sentiment/emotional level; and (3) adheres to generally accepted translator ethics including client confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; sets performance and ethical expectations for written translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: patient care decision support tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Any automated or non-automated tool, mechanism, method, technology, or combination thereof used by a covered entity to support clinical decision-making in its health programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; relevant to §92.210 nondiscrimination in use of such tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: relay interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting from one language to another through an intermediate language, often used for monolingual speakers of languages of limited diffusion; first interpreter renders into an intermediate language, second interpreter interprets into a third language for the speaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §92.4; clarifies acceptable relay processes for languages of limited diffusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances required for applicants and entities
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity applying for Federal financial assistance must submit an assurance (on a form specified by the Director) that the entity's health programs and activities will be operated in compliance with section 1557 and this part. Health insurance issuers seeking Exchange certification or States seeking Exchange approval must submit such assurances. An applicant/entity may incorporate this assurance by reference in subsequent Department applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.5(a); includes requirement as condition of receiving federal assistance or certification/approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and covenants of nondiscrimination assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration of the assurances is the same as for assurances under the Department's regulations implementing section 504; when Federal financial assistance is provided in the form of real property or interest, the same covenants apply as in §84.5(c), except nondiscrimination obligation applies to all bases covered under section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.5(b)-(c); ties assurance duration and property covenants to existing §504 implementation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial action when discrimination is found
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director finds that a recipient or State Exchange has discriminated on the basis of protected characteristics, the recipient/Exchange must take such remedial action as the Director may require to overcome effects of the discrimination. The Director may require remedial action of either or both entities where another recipient exercises control over the discriminator. The Director may require remedial action with respect to persons no longer participants or who would have been participants absent discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.6(a); describes enforcement remedial authority and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary remedial or nondiscriminatory action
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity may take nondiscriminatory steps, in addition to required actions, to overcome effects of conditions that result or resulted in limited participation in its health programs or activities by persons on the basis of protected characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.6(b); encourages proactive measures beyond minimum requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Section 1557 Coordinator (entities with 15+ employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity that employs fifteen or more persons must designate at least one employee as a 'Section 1557 Coordinator' to coordinate compliance with section 1557 and this part in its health programs and activities, including investigating grievances alleging noncompliance. The Coordinator may have designees but must retain ultimate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.7(a); establishes organizational responsibility for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of the Section 1557 Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: At minimum, the Coordinator must: (1) receive, review, and process grievances filed under §92.8(c); (2) coordinate recordkeeping required by §92.8(c); (3) coordinate implementation of language access procedures (§92.8(d)); (4) coordinate implementation of effective communication procedures (§92.8(e)); (5) coordinate implementation of reasonable modification procedures (§92.8(f)); and (6) coordinate training of relevant employees (§92.9) including maintaining documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.7(b); enumerates the Coordinator's core duties for operational compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement for written policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement written policies and procedures in its health programs and activities that are designed to comply with the requirements of this part. The policies/procedures must include an effective date and be reasonably designed, taking into account size, complexity, and type of health programs or activities, to ensure compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.8(a); requires formalized, tailored written compliance documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination policy minimum content
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement a written policy that, at minimum, states the covered entity does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin (including LEP and primary language), sex (consistent with §92.101(a)(2)), age, or disability; that it provides language assistance services and appropriate auxiliary aids and services free of charge when necessary; that it will provide reasonable modifications for individuals with disabilities; and that it provides current contact information for the Section 1557 Coordinator (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: OCR considers it a best practice to state temporary exemptions or assurances of exemption under §92.302(b) in the nondiscrimination policy. Set out in §92.8(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures and recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities with 15+ employees must implement written grievance procedures that provide for prompt and equitable resolution of grievances alleging any action prohibited by section 1557. Such entities must retain records related to grievances alleging discrimination for no less than three calendar years from the date the grievance is resolved; records must include the grievance, complainant contact info (if provided), alleged discriminatory action and basis, filing date, resolution date, grievance resolution, and other pertinent information. Entities must keep the identity of the individual who filed a grievance confidential except as required by law or necessary to carry out this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.8(c)(1)–(3); prescribes content and retention for grievance records and confidentiality protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access procedures minimum content
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement written language access procedures describing the process for providing language assistance services to LEP individuals when required under §92.201. At minimum the procedures must include current contact information for the Section 1557 Coordinator (if applicable); how an employee identifies whether an individual has LEP; how an employee obtains the services of qualified interpreters and translators the covered entity uses; the names of any qualified bilingual staff members; and a list of electronic and written translated materials the covered entity has, the languages they are translated into, date of issuance, and how to access electronic translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.8(d); specifies exact items that must be documented in language access procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective communication procedures for individuals with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement written effective communication procedures describing the covered entity's process for ensuring effective communication for individuals with disabilities when required under §92.202.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §92.8(e); links to auxiliary aids/services definition and the requirement to document processes securing effective communication.
